title: Establishment of Debts and the One-Record Rule — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery Collection Directive
content:
**1. Several debts may be owed at once.** Under **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery**, a beneficiary may owe several debts at once, of the same or different types, with no limit on their number.

**2. Each debt stands alone.** Each overpayment or paid guaranty claim is established as its own debt, with its own notice date, its own balance and its own windows. Debts are never merged.

**3. One originating record, at most one debt.** One originating record creates at most one debt: a debt is established only when no debt already cites the same originating record. The test is made against the system's debt records, whatever the status of the earlier debt (active, on hold, in a repayment plan, referred to Treasury, paid in full, waived or compromised).

**4. Later overpayments on the same record.** Amounts that later prove to be overpaid on the same originating record are added as a new debt with its own notice, not by raising the old balance.

**5. Notice.** When VA establishes a debt it sends the initial notice of rights and obligations; at establishment the debt is active and its balance equals the principal established.

## Points of judgement

| Situation in the records | Result under clauses 3 and 4 |
|---|---|
| No debt cites the originating record | A debt may be established from it |
| A debt already cites the originating record, whatever its status | No second debt is established from that record |
| A further amount later proves overpaid on a record that already has a debt | It becomes a new debt with its own notice; the existing balance is not raised |

**Hypothetical case.** A pension income report produced an overpayment that became a debt, later paid in full. If a further overpayment is later found on that same report, the paid-in-full debt is not reopened or raised: the further amount stands as a new debt with its own notice date, balance and windows.
